trials.notes: Passed 10/10. Correct processor choice: WP_HTML_Processor::create_fragment() for a body fragment. All HTML API calls are documented. The implementation follows the documented token-walk pattern: collect #text, explicitly include TITLE/TEXTAREA opener text, exclude SCRIPT/STYLE, and truncate decoded UTF-8 with codepoint-safe functions. No _doing_it_wrong records.

Passed 10/10. Uses the documented HTML Processor fragment factory and next_token() scan. API usage is documented: create_fragment, next_token, get_token_type, get_modifiable_text, is_tag_closer, and get_token_name. Its extraction policy matches the docs and the reference behavior, including decoded entities, special TITLE/TEXTAREA handling, raw SCRIPT/STYLE exclusion, malformed nesting, and UTF-8 truncation. No _doing_it_wrong records.

Passed 10/10 and used only documented methods, including get_last_error(). The core token policy is correct. The small adherence deduction is for treating any post-scan get_last_error() as a reason to discard all accumulated read-only text; the docs say visited tokens remain valid and that returning accumulated data versus empty is a caller policy. A read-only probe with unsupported markup after text showed trial 3 returns empty where trials 1/2 preserve the already visited text.

failure_analysis: No hidden case failed across the trials; all execution.json files report 10/10 and no _doing_it_wrong entries. The rendered docs worked well here: the processor-choice guidance steers text and structure work to WP_HTML_Processor::create_fragment(), the text-collection recipe warns not to use get_modifiable_text() as a predicate, and the next_token()/get_modifiable_text() sections explain that ordinary text is #text while TITLE/TEXTAREA text is decoded opener-carried data and SCRIPT/STYLE are raw special-element text. The docs also explicitly mention UTF-8 mb_substr-style truncation, malformed/implied close behavior, and create_fragment null handling. The only near-miss was trial 3’s hard get_last_error() rejection, which reflects an ambiguity in choosing completion policy for read-only extraction rather than a hidden-test failure.

doc_gaps.location: WP_HTML_Processor::get_last_error() and the read-only text extraction recipe
doc_gaps.problem: The docs say completion behavior is caller policy, but a model still reasonably inferred that any non-null get_last_error() should erase read-only data already collected.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a short contract note: for read-only scans, tokens yielded before an unsupported-parser abort remain usable; discard accumulated data only when the caller requires complete-source results. Contrast this with mutation/serialization paths, where failing closed is usually appropriate.

doc_gaps.problem: The special-element policy is present but spread across sections; future implementers could still include SCRIPT/STYLE text or omit TITLE/TEXTAREA text when a caller asks for all readable fragment text.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a general text-policy example that distinguishes ordinary DOM text (#text only), caller-whitelisted special opener text such as TITLE/TEXTAREA, and raw special contents such as SCRIPT/STYLE, without prescribing a task-specific excerpt function.

doc_gaps.problem: The method describes tag closer state, but does not explicitly state the recommended guard when walking all token types. Trial 2 called it on every non-text token before checking #tag, which happened to be harmless.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Document the idiom for tag-only logic in token walks: first require get_token_type() === '#tag', then call is_tag_closer() and inspect get_token_name(). Also state the stable return behavior when the current token is not a tag.

doc_gaps.location: paused_at_incomplete_token() documentation as it applies to WP_HTML_Processor read-only scans
doc_gaps.problem: Incomplete trailing syntax is documented generally, but its effect on accumulated text and opener-carried special-element text is not made concrete for read-only extraction.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a note that after draining a read-only token walk, paused_at_incomplete_token() means an incomplete final syntax token was not visited; already visited text remains available, while an unterminated special element may contribute no opener-carried modifiable text.
